_comment: A whole install, as Notion returned it, on 2026-08-18. Six databases created, thirteen relations added, seven views built, then every data source and database fetched back and transcribed here. The viewRows and sqlRows are the second half of the proof: each view was queried in view mode, the same rule was run as SQL against the data source, and the two sets of rows are what is recorded. This is a record of what Notion does, not of what the design hoped it would do. Two transcription notes: the propertyUrl values are shortened, because verify only asks whether one is present, that being what separates a two-way relation from a one-way one; and the shared option lists were read back identically in every database that carries them, checked in each fetch rather than assumed. The Notion ids in this file are stand-ins. The real ones point at throwaway databases in a private workspace and this repository is public, so each was replaced with a fixed placeholder, consistently, so that every relation still points where it pointed. Nothing else was altered. KNOWN GAPS, recorded 2026-08-18 rather than patched, because this file is a record and not a wish. (1) It predates the description on Software.Contract link, which was added to schema.js after this install ran, so that property comes back with no description here while the current manifest asks for one. (2) No property in this file carries a `description` key at all, and that is a transcription gap rather than what Notion does: fetching the live Projects and Software data sources on 2026-08-18 returned `description` on every single property, empty string where there is none. (3) viewRows and sqlRows hold page TITLES, and the rule query now selects `url`, because titles are not unique. Re-record all three by re-running an install and fetching it back.
